阻塞整个事件循环\n    return response\n```\n\n3. 模型调用执行期间，**所有其他 FastAPI 端点均无响应**（健康检查、WebSocket 连接等全部挂起）。\n\n**期望行为**\n\n多模态路径应使用 `await dashscope.AioMultiModalConversation.call()`（DashScope SDK 已提供），避免阻塞 asyncio 事件循环，与非多模态路径行为保持一致。\n\n**根因分析**\n\n[src/agentscope/model/_dashscope_model.py](cci:7://file:///D:/work/worknote/project/TeachingAnalyzer/agentscope/src/agentscope/model/_dashscope_model.py:0:0-0:0) 第 273 行：\n\n```python\n# 当前代码（阻塞）：\nresponse = dashscope.MultiModalConversation.call(\n    api_key=self.api_key,\n    **kwargs,\n)\n\n# 期望代码（非阻塞）：\nresponse = await dashscope.AioMultiModalConversation.call(\n    api_key=self.api_key,\n    **kwargs,\n)\n```\n\n两个 API 签名完全一致，唯一区别：\n- `MultiModalConversation.call()` → 同步函数，返回 `Response | Generator`\n- `AioMultiModalConversation.call()` → 异步协程，返回 `Response | AsyncGenerator`\n\n下游 [_parse_dashscope_stream_response](cci:1://file:///d:/work/worknote/project/Professional%20evaluation/agentscope/src/agentscope/model/_dashscope_model.py:299:4-477:13) 的类型标注已包含 `Union[AsyncGenerator, Generator]`，因此修改应该是向后兼容的。\n\n**错误信息**\n\n无显式错误信息。表现为 asyncio 事件循环被阻塞，导致所有并发异步任务（HTTP 处理器、WebSocket 连接、后台任务）在同步 API 调用完成前全部停滞。\n\n**环境信息：**\n\n- AgentScope 版本：1.0.16\n- Python 版本：3.11.14\n- 操作系统：Windows 11\n- DashScope SDK 版本：最新\n\n**补充说明**\n\n- 同步 MultiModalConversation.call() 调用在 PR #1215 之前就已存在（用于 qvq/-vl 模型名自动检测场景）。PR #1215 添加了 multimodality 参数使其可显式控制，但未将底层调用更新为异步版本 AioMultiModalConversation.call()，使得该同步阻塞问题扩展到了更多模型场景。\n- 修复仅需一行代码：将 `dashscope.MultiModalConversation.call(` 替换为 `await dashscope.AioMultiModalConversation.call(`。\n- 目前我们通过 `asyncio.run_in_executor()` 将同步调用放入线程池作为临时方案，但这增加了不必要的复杂性。\n",

[`post_model_hook_router`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/2553ae0b877c58beb8947db70336c008d7c7ea23/libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py#L709) decides if a tool execution is required, and will use `Send` to route to the tool node like so:\n```python\nreturn [Send(\"tools\", [tool_call]) for tool_call in pending_tool_calls]\n```\n\nComparing that with the [`should_continue`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/2553ae0b877c58beb8947db70336c008d7c7ea23/libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py#L632) implementation, When there is no \"post_model_hook\" setup it will `Send` to the tools node like so:\n```python\ntool_calls = [\n    tool_node.inject_tool_args(call, state, store)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n    for call in last_message.tool_calls\n]\nreturn [Send(\"tools\", [tool_call]) for tool_call in tool_calls]\n```\n\nSo, when the hook is setup you get the flow:\nagent -> should_continue -> post_model_hook -> post_model_hook_router -> tools\nAnd without you get:\nagent -> should_continue -> tools\n\nThe first, will neglect to inject a state/store and the latter will.\nI believe this is a bug.\nIdeally, there will be a single \"send to tools\" implementation which both routers should use.\n\n### System Info\n\nSystem Information\n------------------\n> OS:  Darwin\n> OS Version:  Darwin Kernel Version We decorated agent/task methods with `async def` to support `await self._create_tools()`\n2. The `@agent`, `@task`, `@crew` decorators don't await the async methods\n3. This returns a coroutine object instead of Agent/Task/Crew instances\n4. When CrewAI tries to access `.name` attribute on the coroutine, it fails\n\n### Error Stack\n```\nERROR | src.agents.tools.base:run_crew_isolated:141 - Crew execution failed | \ncrew_class=FounderCrew run_mode=answer error='coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'\n\nTraceback:\n  File \"src/agents/tools/base.py\", line 135, in run_crew_isolated\n    result = crew_instance.crew(run_mode).kickoff_async(inputs)\nAttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'\n```\n\n## Workaround Attempted\nWe tried wrapping async `_arun()` calls in a sync `_run()` fallback:\n\n```python\ndef _run(self, *args, **kwargs):\n    return run_async(self._arun(*args, **kwargs))  # ❌ Creates new event loop → loop conflicts\n```\n\nThis reintroduces \"Task got Future attached to a different loop\" errors because it spawns a new event loop inside the existing one.\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\nThe `@agent`, `@task`, and `@crew` decorators use class method introspection but don't check if the method is a coroutine function. They should either:\n\n1. **Auto-await async methods** (recommended for modern Python):\n```python\ndef decorator(method):\n    def wrapper(self):\n        result = method(self)\n        if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):\n            return asyncio.run(result)  # Or: await result in async context\n        return result\n    return wrapper\n```\n\n2. **Explicitly reject async methods** with helpful error:\n```python\ndef decorator(method):\n    if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(method):\n        raise TypeError(\n            f\"Method '{method.__name__}' is async but @agent/@task/@crew \"\n            \"decorators only support sync methods. \"\n            \"Create tools synchronously or use a different pattern.\"\n        )\n    return original_decorator(method)\n```\n\n## Questions for CrewAI Team\n1. Are `@agent`, `@task`, `@crew` decorators intentionally limited to sync-only?\n2. Is there a supported pattern for async tool creation in async-first applications?\n3. Would a PR adding async support to decorators be welcome?\n4. Should we await async methods at decoration time or at call time?\n\n## Production Context\nThis is a production issue affecting:\n- **Telegram Bot** (aiogram) with async handlers\n- **FastAPI** application with async endpoints  \n- **AsyncSQLAlchemy** database operations\n- **PostgreSQL** via asyncpg driver\n\nWe need async-safe tool execution to avoid event loop conflicts and zombie database connections.\n\n## Proposed Solution\nAdd async method detection and auto-await to the decorators:\n\n```python\n# In crewai/decorators.py or similar\nimport asyncio\nfrom functools import wraps\n\ndef agent(method):\n    @wraps(method)\n    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):\n        result = method(self, *args, **kwargs)\n        if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):\n            # Option 1: Run in current event loop (if in async context)\n            try:\n                loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()\n                # Schedule as task if already in event loop\n                return asyncio.ensure_future(result)\n            except RuntimeError:\n                # No running loop - run new one\n                return asyncio.run(result)\n        return result\n    return wrapper\n```\n\nThis allows developers to write naturally async code while maintaining backward compatibility.\n\n### Steps to Reproduce\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n### Code Example\n```python\nfrom crewai import Agent, Task, Crew\nfrom crewai.task import Task\nfrom crewai.agent import Agent\n\nclass FounderCrew:\n    @agent\n    async def your-agent(self) -> Agent:\n        \"\"\"This is the problem - decorators don't support async\"\"\"\n        tools = await self._create_tools()  # Async operation\n        return Agent(\n            config=self.agents_config[\"your-agent\"],\n            tools=tools,\n        )\n    \n    @task\n    async def your-agent(self) -> Task:\n        \"\"\"Task method with async\"\"\"\n        return Task(\n            config=self.tasks_config[\"your-agent\"],\n        )\n    \n    @crew\n    async def crew(self, run_mode: str = \"answer\") -> Crew:\n        \"\"\"Crew method with async/await\"\"\"\n        tasks = [await self. your-agent()]\n        agents = [await self. your-agent()]\n        return Crew(agents=agents, tasks=tasks, process=Process.sequential)\n\n# Called from FastAPI/Telegram async handler\nresult = await crew.crew(run_mode=\"answer\").kickoff_async(inputs={})\n```\n\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nI think when I use the kickoff_async(), it should call the tools using _arun() by default, or should I create tools in async ? \n\n## Expected Behavior\n- `@agent`, `@task`, and `@crew` decorators should either:\n  1. Support async methods natively by awaiting them, OR\n  2. Raise a clear error message stating async is not supported, OR\n  3. Provide documentation and recommended patterns for async tool creation\n\n## Actual Behavior\n- Decorators return unawaited coroutine objects\n- Causes cascading `AttributeError` when CrewAI tries to access object properties\n- No clear error message indicating the problem is with async decorator usage\n\n\n### Screenshots/Code snippets\n\n<img width=\"755\" height=\"716\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c04a7f68-5c9b-4ac4-b54f-b3441d37083d\" />\n\n<img width=\"660\" height=\"183\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8446d13-132d-4995-bcad-a8e89451ade7\" />\n\n<img width=\"540\" height=\"161\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a128449e-ba11-4ae9-8b50-1d8c150f2aab\" />\n\n<img width=\"664\" height=\"174\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0865753c-4ceb-4215-a49c-c4bb149e0174\" />\n\n### Operating System\n\nUbuntu 20.04\n\n### Python Version\n\n3.12\n\n### crewAI Version\n\ncrewai==1.4.1\n\n### crewAI Tools Version\n\ncrewai-tools==1.4.1\n\n### Virtual Environment\n\nVenv\n\n### Evidence\n\n.\n\n### Possible Solution\n\n.\n\n### Additional context\n\n.\n",

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│                  Key Findings for Dockerfile Fix                   │
│                                                                    │
│  1 PostgreSQL Version Mismatch: The error references PostgreSQL 14 │
│    (/etc/postgresql/14/main/), but the repository uses PostgreSQL  │
│    16. The Dockerfile should use postgres:16 instead of any        │
│    PostgreSQL 14 references.                                       │
│  2 Correct PostgreSQL Setup: The proper way to set up PostgreSQL   │
│    for tests is using Docker Compose with the provided             │
│    compose-postgres.yml file, not manual initdb commands.          │
│  3 Alternative for Dockerfile: If PostgreSQL must be installed in  │
│    the Dockerfile (not as a separate container), use:              │
│     • PostgreSQL 16 (not 14)                                       │
│     • Proper initialization using pg_createcluster instead of      │
│       initdb (as suggested by the test_analysis_agent)             │
│     • Or simply use the postgres:16 Docker image as a service      │
│  4 Test Execution: Tests can run without PostgreSQL for basic      │
│    cases (using "memory" or "sqlite" checkpointer options), but    │
│    full test coverage requires PostgreSQL via the fixtures.        │
